title: The image of the invisible God (Colossians 1:15–20)
word: The image of the invisible God
hook: an early hymn: in him all things hold together
tomorrow: rooted and built up: why does Paul mix a tree and a house?

segments.voice: That was the week of the house: people made on purpose, a wall brought down, a prayer on the knees, seven ones, a deadline on anger, and armor for standing. Yesterday's line was one word: stand.

A photo of someone you've never met still tells you things: the face, the smile, the way they hold their shoulders. A new letter, to believers in a small town called Colosse, says something much bolder about Jesus: "Who is the image of the invisible God." A face you can look at, of someone nobody can see. And then the lines start to swing and balance, like a song.
screen: `A PHOTO OF SOMEONE YOU'VE NEVER MET.` → `THE IMAGE OF THE INVISIBLE GOD.` → `THE LINES START TO SING.`

segments.voice: Some readers think Paul is quoting a hymn the churches already sang. The letter doesn't say. Christians read the first line this way: look at Jesus, and you see what God is like. Then the song widens as far as it can go: "For by him were all things created, that are in heaven, and that are in earth, visible and invisible." Then one short line: "And he is before all things, and by him all things consist." Consist, in the King James, means hold together. Here's one to tell a friend: the verse isn't only about a beginning. It's about right now. Not made once and left on a shelf, but held. Then the song comes close: he is "the head of the body, the church," "the firstborn from the dead." And it ends where this whole stretch of letters keeps ending, in peace: God is "to reconcile all things unto himself," having "made peace through the blood of his cross." Listen to the phrase that keeps coming back: all things. Made, held, reconciled. No corner left out.
screen: `A HYMN? THE LETTER DOESN'T SAY.` · `ALL THINGS CREATED.` · `BY HIM ALL THINGS CONSIST.` · `ALL THINGS RECONCILED.` · then, large: `ALL THINGS HOLD TOGETHER.`

segments.voice: Walk slowly through one room for a minute, noticing what holds it together: a hinge, a seam, a nail, a photo of people you love. Then sit, and name the one thing, or the one person, who held your day together.
The image of the invisible God. Colossians' words for Jesus: a face you can look at, of a God nobody can see.
screen: `THE IMAGE OF THE INVISIBLE GOD — today's word`.

segments.voice: The line to keep: all things hold together, held right now, not just made once. Two weeks of letters, done.

fork.setup: a kid in your Sunday school class asks: 'if nobody can see God, how do Christians know what God is like?' what fits Colossians 1?

fork.reveal: Christians read Colossians 1:15 as: look at Jesus, and you see what God is like. a sentence a parent could say at dinner.

chat.says: it HAPPENED. dad and i made up, pop and hermana luz washed dishes together. how do we keep this?
options: It's not all on you: in him all things hold together. Ask both churches for one more date.
Hold it together yourself; if you stop pushing, the whole thing falls apart.

chat.meaning: Colossians 1:17: by him all things consist, hold together. Held right now, not by one person's effort; Grace can keep going without carrying it all.
